chapter: New Orleans dance scene of the 1920s
title: Midnight shows at the Palace and Robichaux's pit band
summary: Friday midnight shows for white audiences with blues singers and a pit band led by Robichaux, the fiddler.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You want to talk about the midnight shows now?

Well, I was thinking about the midnight shows at the Old Palace, I think it was, and the shows were, of course, for Negroes all during the week. It was a sort of a vaudeville circuit similar to the off-human circuits of that side except when it was Negroes. And each Friday night there was a midnight show for white people. And we, of course, tried never to miss it because, in addition to having a very good orchestra pit band, there were many good acts and good singers. I can recall hearing, for instance, Ethel Waters, Sarah Martin, Esther Bijou, some of the Smith sisters. There were so many of them. Not Bessie, of course. I didn't hear Bessie there, but I think Mamie Smith and some of the others. And there was a very fine drummer with this pit band. I don't recall his name.
What did he look like? Was he dark or light or...?
As I recall, rather on the short side and dark, yes. But I don't recall his name.
And which band was this at the minute?
The fiddler or the piano player?
The fiddler. That's about all of that.
